title: Finance & Legal: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Playbook (Q1 2025)
author: Marisol Ortega
body:
Overview

This playbook documents Redwood Inference's standard processes and operational controls for budgeting & forecasting, procurement & contract approvals, and revenue recognition & billing. The purpose is to provide a single, executable reference for finance, legal, procurement, and partnering stakeholders to ensure consistent execution, compliance, and predictable financial reporting.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood business units and legal entities unless a written exception is approved by Finance (CFO) and Legal.
- Covers annual budgeting, quarterly/monthly forecasting cadence, procurement approvals (software, hardware, vendor services), contract lifecycle touchpoints, and revenue recognition rules used by accounting and RevOps.

Principles

1. Central accountability: Finance (FP&A) owns budgeting and forecast consolidation; Legal owns contract language and risk appetite; Procurement coordinates supplier onboarding and vendor controls.
2. Segregation of duties: Approval workflows must separate requestors, approvers, and payment owners.
3. Materiality: Items over defined thresholds require additional approvals and documentation (see thresholds table).
4. Auditability: All material decisions must be recorded in the procurement system and linked to budget/GL codes.

Key Roles and Responsibilities

- FP&A (Budget Owner): Consolidate departmental budgets, run variance analysis, provide forecast guidance.
- Accounting/RevRec: Maintain revenue recognition policy and post billing entries.
- Legal: Review and approve contract terms and exceptions.
- Procurement: Manage vendor onboarding, PO issuance, and contract repository.
- Department Leaders: Own line-item budgets, approve spend within delegated authority.

Budgeting and Forecasting Process (Annual + Rolling Forecast)

1. Annual Budget (timeline):
   1) Kickoff (T-14 weeks): FP&A sends template and baseline model to department leads.
   2) Bottom-up build (T-12 to T-8 weeks): Departments submit detailed line items, hiring plans, and capital requests.
   3) Consolidation (T-7 to T-4 weeks): FP&A aggregates inputs, runs scenario analysis (base, upside, downside).
   4) Leadership review (T-3 to T-2 weeks): Execs review trade-offs, headcount plans, and capital allocations.
   5) Board & Finance approval (T-1 week): Final budget submitted for approval and published.

2. Rolling Forecasting (quarterly cadence with monthly updates):
   - Owners update forecast monthly in the planning tool with commentary on material variances (>5% for a line).
   - FP&A issues updated rolling 12-month forecast each month and a deep-dive forecast prior to quarter close.

3. Budget Change Requests (BCR):
   - For net new commitments or re-allocations >= $50k, submit a BCR form with business justification, savings/ROI, and counterbalancing reductions.
   - Approval matrix: Department head (<= $100k), Finance director (<= $500k), CFO (> $500k).

Material Thresholds and Delegations

| Threshold | Approver | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| <$5k | Dept Lead | Operational purchases; no PO required for recurring committed services under $5k/mo if pre-approved in budget. |
| $5k - $50k | Procurement Manager + Dept Lead | PO required. Standard T&C apply. |
| $50k - $500k | Finance Director + Legal (commercial review) | Contract review mandatory; BCR required. |
| > $500k | CFO + Legal + Procurement Director | Executive approval and, for multi-year commitments, additional capex evaluation. |

Procurement and Vendor Onboarding Workflow

Step-by-step: 
1. Request initiation: Requestor files a procurement request in the procurement system (fields: business justification, budget code, estimated spend, requested vendor).
2. Procurement triage: Procurement validates budget availability and determines required diligence (security/compliance, SOC2/ISO attestation, data residency).
3. Legal review: Legal performs contract review using standard templates; high-risk terms (data rights, indemnities, termination for convenience) flagged for senior counsel.
4. PO issuance: Once contract signed, Procurement issues PO referencing contract ID and GL codes.
5. Vendor onboarding: Security and Infrastructure complete any technical assessment (if vendor will handle customer data or integrate with infrastructure).

Required Documentation Checklist (minimum for award):
- Approved procurement request with budget code and owner
- Executed contract or signed SOW
- Vendor W9 / contractual tax forms (for US vendors)
- Security questionnaire or SOC2 report (if applicable)
- PO number and GL mapping

Contract Review Standards

- Use Redwood standard SaaS and services templates as first preference. Templates contain: term, termination, IP assignment, confidentiality, liability caps, and data protection addendum.
- Commercial deviations: Document proposed deviations in the contract deviation log and capture business justification and risk mitigation.
- Contract lifecycle owners: Legal (primary), Requesting team (secondary), Procurement (administrative).

Revenue Recognition and Billing Policy (High-level Guidance)

1. Revenue streams covered: Hosted API usage, Dedicated reserved capacity contracts, Private deployment licensing & support, Professional services (implementation & integration), Observability and add-ons.
2. Recognition principles (aligned to ASC 606 / IFRS 15):
   - Identify contract(s) with a customer.
   - Identify performance obligations (e.g., access to hosted API, delivery of on-prem package, professional services milestones).
   - Determine the transaction price (including variable consideration such as usage fees or credits).
   - Allocate the transaction price to performance obligations.
   - Recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied.

3. Typical treatment examples: 
   - Hosted API usage: Recognize as revenue as tokens are consumed (usage-based, recognized over time).
   - Reserved capacity (Dedicated): If billed upfront for a term, recognize ratably over the term unless there is a separate upfront deliverable.
   - Private deployments (license + support): Allocate license (if distinct) and recognize per license policy; support recognized over the support term.
   - Professional services: Recognize based on milestones or time-and-materials as services are delivered.

4. Billing cadence and invoicing policies:
   - Usage billing: Monthly in arrears with 30-day payment terms unless otherwise negotiated.
   - Reserved/commitments: Typically invoiced quarterly or annually in advance per contract.
   - Dispute handling: RevOps captures billing disputes in BillingOps queue; Finance retains disputed amounts in a suspense account until resolution.

5. Revenue cut-off and month-end close responsibilities:
   - RevOps provides usage files to Accounting by Day+3 (three business days after month end).
   - Accounting runs recognition process and posts revenue by Day+7. Any manual adjustments documented with reconciliations and approvals.

Operational Controls, SLOs, and Audit Points

- PO issuance SLA: Procurement issues PO within 5 business days of a fully approved contract and completed onboarding checklist.
- Contract review SLA: Standard contracts reviewed within 5 business days; high-risk deals (enterprise, > $250k) within 10 business days with prioritized counsel.
- Forecast accuracy target: Rolling 12-month forecast to be within +/- 3% of actuals for direct costs and +/- 5% for revenue across the fiscal year.
- Billing data integrity: Error rate on usage aggregation must be <0.2% monthly.

Templates and Examples

- Budget template: (CSV/Excel) includes line-item mapping to chart-of-accounts, headcount plan, and hiring timeline.
- BCR form: standard web form URL (internal) + required attachments (cost model, impact).
- Procurement request form: fields: title, vendor, justification, budget owner, estimated ARR/TCV, GL code.

Example: Procurement Request Table
| Field | Example | Required |
|---|---|---|
| Title | "OpenSearch fleet upgrade" | Yes |
| Vendor | Acme Cloud Services | Yes |
| Estimated spend | $220,000 (annual) | Yes |
| Security posture | SOC2 Type II available | Conditional |
| Budget code | ENG-OPS-2025 | Yes |

Dispute and Exception Handling

- Exceptions to this playbook (e.g., accelerated procurement for SOC incidents, one-time emergency purchases) require an emergency exception form and post-facto approval by CFO and Head of Legal within 7 business days.
- Contract deviations that increase legal risk beyond standard templates must be logged and a mitigation plan posted to the contract file.

Appendix A — Quick Reference Checklists (copy into procurement system)

1) New Vendor Checklist (minimum)
   - Signed contract / SOW
   - PO issued
   - Tax form collected
   - Security review or documented exemption

2) Revenue Recognition Quick Matrix
   - Usage fees -> Recognize over-time at usage reporting interval
   - Prepaid subscriptions -> Recognize ratably over contract term
   - Professional services (fixed price) -> Recognize at milestone if deliverables distinct
